summary: Dedicated GPU pool throughput drop and noisy-neighbor symptoms during autoscale events
description:
Issue summary:
Customer CobaltAI reported a sharp drop in dedicated capacity throughput and intermittent 5xx/timeout errors for long-running chat sessions. Impact: customer-reported latency up from median 120ms to 1.8s and 15-30% failed requests across a handful of production routes.

Impact:
- Multiple production endpoints experienced throttled concurrency and timeouts during peak traffic (12:30-15:00 UTC).
- Customer reports an increase in token costs due to retries.

Environment:
- Dedicated GPU pool (dedicated-cobalt-pool), prod, us-east primary, us-west failover.
- Autoscaler configured with min_replicas=4, max_replicas=16, cool_down=300s, scale_metric=average_gpu_utilization.

Steps to reproduce (provided by customer):
1) Run steady stream of mixed short-chat and long-context stream requests at ~400 req/s across 6 routes pinned to dedicated-cobalt-pool.
2) Observe request latencies and 5xx spike after ~20 minutes when batch sizes for long-context requests increase.

Observed behavior:
- Throughput dipped by 45% for pinned routes when autoscaler attempted scaling (scale up triggered but new nodes joined slowly).
- Node-level GPU memory pressure and sporadic driver timeouts appeared in logs.
- Support saw bursty GPU SM utilization but not sustained average utilization, so autoscaler did not react quickly.

Expected behavior:
- Autoscaler should add capacity before request latency and 5xxs increase or fall back cleanly to hosted variants per routing policy.

Logs & metrics included:
- Attached grafana links and excerpts showing GPU memory used, SM utilization, queue length, and autoscaler decision events.
- Kernel driver warnings and gpuscheduler backpressure traces included in attachments.

investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Noisy neighbor - one tenant's long-lived, high-batch inference jobs saturate GPU memory and cause kernel stalls. Evidence: host-level NVML logs show repeated BAR1 read slowdowns during incident window.

Hypothesis 2: Autoscaler metric mismatch - scaling uses 5m average GPU SM util; bursty peak causes queueing without being observable to autoscaler. Evidence: 1m percentile util shows spikes >90% while 5m average remains ~48%.

Hypothesis 3: Slow instance provisioning - warmup/initialization for new instances takes longer under memory pressure leading to delayed capacity arrival. Evidence: join latency for new nodes increased from median 30s to 180s during incident.

Investigative actions: collected NVML traces, gpuscheduler logs, autoscaler decision events, instance bootstrap logs, and tenant routing assignments. Conducted controlled repro with mixed workload; reproduced tail latencies and failure modes.
Observed correlation between large KV cache sessions (long-context chat) and persistent GPU memory fragmentation leading to driver reset attempts on older driver stack.
resolution_notes: Short-term mitigation: Increased min_replicas for dedicated-cobalt-pool from 4 to 6, created a placement group to avoid noisy-neighbor co-location with heavy internal jobs, and applied autoscaler hotfix (cooldown=90s + queue-length override). Migrated CobaltAI traffic at 2026-02-23T16:40Z.

Root cause: Combination of noisy-neighbor long-batch sessions causing GPU memory fragmentation and a scaling policy that averaged utilization over too long a window. This prevented timely autoscaling and allowed queue growth and kernel stalls.

Permanent fixes planned: 1) Update autoscaler to include 1m p95 GPU util and queue-length signals (PR merged https://github.com/redwood-inference/autoscaler/pull/214). 2) Adjust scheduler placement rules to prefer isolation for large-memory workloads. 3) Improve instance bootstrap parallelism and pre-warm images to reduce join latency. 4) Customer guidance: recommend pinning heavy batch workloads to separate sub-pool or using Dedicated burst capacity for predictable throughput.
Follow-ups: schedule postmortem (owner: Ibrahim Khan) due 2026-02-28, update runbook and customer-facing KB article, monitor other dedicated pools for similar signs.
resolution: Mitigated - customer migrated to isolated placement group, autoscaler hotfix deployed, and pool min_replicas increased. Ongoing monitoring and postmortem scheduled.
customer_impact_summary: CobaltAI experienced elevated latencies and 15-30% request failures for pinned routes during peak. Incident reduced token efficiency and caused business-impacting errors for production users. Post-mitigation errors below 2%.
next_steps: Complete postmortem, merge autoscaler metric improvements, update runbooks, offer CobaltAI guidance on workload isolation and reserved burst capacity, and run a scheduled audit of other dedicated pools for noisy-neighbor indicators.
